stem:
Examination of the Eye (theory notes, bulleted):
• Anterior chamber and the iris posteriorly. The iris lies between the back surface of the cornea anteriorly.
• Posterior chamber lies between the back surface of the iris anteriorly and the crystalline lens posteriorly.
• Iris is the colored portion of the eye.
• The pupil is jet-black in the newborn and starts to acquire a greyish tinge as the person gets older due to the continuous addition of new lens fibers throughout life causing light scattering; a process known as senile sclerosis. It is to be noted that in the absence of the lens (surgically removed or posteriorly dislocated), the pupil regains its jet-black color.

Theory notes (bulleted), continuation of Examination of the Eye:
• Ciliary body has 3 functions (3 As) as follows:
•Accommodation for near and far vision through the effect of contraction and relaxation of the ciliary muscle transmitted to the lens via the zonules (discussed in detail in the 2 notes below).
•Aqueous humor secretion.
•Attachment to the zonular fibers keeping the lens in place.
• When the ciliary muscle relaxes, the zonules become taut (tense), resulting in flattening of the lens, and hence improving the focus for far objects (distant vision).
• Conversely, when the ciliary muscle contracts, the zonules become relaxed, and consequently, the lens becomes more convex, improving the focus for near objects (accommodation).
• Photoreceptor cells in the retina are of two types as follows:
•Rods: Necessary for seeing in dim (faint) light.
•Cones: Necessary for sharp vision, day vision, and color vision.
